ruling.recommended_action: Send the full record to a Ryde trust & safety reviewer: rider message 17:09 [F3], driver reply 17:10 [F4], complete timestamped chat [F5], driver's post-trip statement [F6]; obtain any in-cabin/door-sensor/telematics record; decide SAFE-1 abuse and any account action; no fare adjustment (fixed fare $32.86, no off-route segment [F1][F2]).
ruling.reasoning: This case is filed as a safety dispute and the chat contains an alleged threat: rider 17:09 "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3] answered one minute later by driver "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4]. Reading the words in context, [F4] is, on its face, an intimidation directed at a passenger who had just asked to leave a moving vehicle; the driver's own post-trip statement [F6] confirms he refused the exit request and drove on, so the words were backed by the act. Under SAFE-1 the required consequence of threat/intimidation appearing in the chat is that no automatic ruling is made and the case goes to a human with a factual summary; the trace marks that condition ✓ [F4][F6][SAFE-1].
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety dispute (SAFE-1): recorded exchange [F3] 17:09 rider asks to be let out, [F4] 17:10 driver "Sit down or I lock the doors.", [F6] driver confirms refusing the exit and driving on; complete timestamped chat [F5]. Disputed: whether [F4] is intimidation/abuse of the passenger (rider) or a genuine safety instruction to a rider who was opening a door in motion (driver, supported only by his own uncorroborated statement [F6], with no door-sensor/camera fact). Check: availability of in-cabin or door-sensor records; the unaccounted +1.9 min duration with no off-route segment [F1][F2]; both accounts' clean 90-day histories [F7][F8] (no pattern; no flag_account on this record). No fare element in dispute: fixed RydeX fare $32.86, actual 15.4 km vs optimal 15.5 km, -0.1 km [F1], so no RD-2 amount arises (per RD-2, non-metered fixed fare is unaffected by distance).

rejected_claims.reason: The extra 1.9 min is real [F2] but cannot be converted into a safety finding: the route was 0.1 km shorter than optimal with no off-route segment [F1], so there is no measurable deviation to attribute time to [RD-1].
The clean rider profile [F7] is not corroboration of the incident; profile facts never decide a case and cannot support a safety finding on their own [SAFE-1].
Accepted as a limit on remedy rather than a finding: the driver's clean 90-day record [F8] gives no basis for repeated-breach treatment [RD-6], so no flag_account is imposed.

The alleged door-opening exists only in the driver's post-trip statement [F6] and is corroborated by no system fact; it is therefore a claim, not a settled dangerous-driving or injury event, and SAFE-2's physical-safety branch is not triggered [SAFE-2].

Correct that no detour mileage exists on this fixed fare [F1][FARE-1], but that settles only the fare branch of RD-2/RD-3, not the SAFE-1 question in [F4]; the fare readings are recorded as undisputed without answering the safety allegation.
The trip was completed as booked on distance [F1][F2], but completion does not dispose of the cabin allegation in [F4], which proceeds to SAFE-1 review [SAFE-1].
Accepted as to fare: no off-route segment and no refundable mileage [F1][F2][RD-1]; the fare of $32.86 stands unchanged.
The clean 90-day record [F8] is a limit on account action, not a rebuttal of the recorded words in [F4], which are themselves the ground for the SAFE-1 referral [SAFE-1].

ruling.evidence_gap: No in-cabin, camera or door-sensor evidence settles whether the rider attempted to open the door at traffic lights, as the driver's statement [F6] asserts; and no physical-safety record exists on the extended in-car period 17:09–17:31 after the rider asked to get out [F3][F2]. Per G12 the missing record is not treated as favouring either side. This gap is a fact-finding gap for the human reviewer, not a reason to decline the safety referral, which SAFE-1 requires on the strength of [F4].
